body: Note that my pull request just improves the error message xcode_configure.bzl is printing.  It does not address anything about AppleConfiguration being overzealous about XCode existing.
Our mac tests (bazel_objc_test, bazel_apple_test) rely on iOS SDK being present, which you only get with Xcode installed. I can only guess that that is why Xcode presence is assumed.
Is there anyway to get around this error? I am getting the exact same error as op on my macbook air. I do not have Xcode, but do have command line tools. I am unable to install bazel.
FWIW, you can install Bazel using the binary installer (e.g., https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/releases/tag/0.3.1), you just can't build bazel.

Following your suggestion, I installed bazel for macosx using the installer. However, I get the following error when trying to use bazel to build tensorflow from the source. 

gcc: error: unrecognized command line option '-Wthread-safety'
gcc: error: unrecognized command line option '-Wself-assign'

The exact same problem was  reported in #649 , where  you  suggested to edit CROSSTOOL but I am unable to do that since I did not build bazel from the source. 

Do you have any other suggestions to resolve this error? Thanks a lot.

Add the following to your WORKSPACE file:

```
local_repository(
    name = "bazel_tools",
    path = "/path/to/the/bazel/source/tree"
)
```

Then edit the CROSSTOOL file in `/path/to/the/bazel/source/tree/tools/cpp/CROSSTOOL`.
I added those lines to WORKSPACE file (from tensorflow source tree) and updated CROSSTOOL (bazel source tree), however I still get the same error.
